knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Permission is obtained and the lift is isolated with the doors open, so the worker is not in a confined space and the car is safe to enter. Pressing a call button or dismantling the panel is not part of the procedure.
The buttons are touched by many people, so they must be hygienic. During the clean, no call button may be pressed, because that could bring the lift into use.
Opening the shaft or working on mechanisms is outside the lesson. Car walls, handrails, doors, tracks, the vacuum check and the floor are within scope.

practicalCriteria: Learner confirms permission with the building contact on a supplied scenario card, and states the isolation step before entering the car.
Learner selects a material for each supplied lift surface (walls, handrail, doors, control panel, floor, tracks) from the approved list, and states the reason for each choice.
Learner cleans a supplied lift car mock-up without pressing any call button, keeping liquid out of the panel.
Learner checks the car and landing for equipment and waste before returning the lift to service, and records the job.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Permission and timing record from the building contact
Assessor observation of the lift mock-up clean
Isolation and return-to-service record with time
stopWorkCriteria: Lift does not isolate or return to service as the procedure requires
A call button activates during the work
Any task inside the shaft, pit or machine room is requested or started
